spec_features.feature_name: minimize gratuitous harm at near-zero cost
spec_features.spec_quote: treats that uncertainty seriously and minimizes gratuitous harm at near-zero cost to the science
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella claim is realized by the concrete mechanisms that DO run: the max_turns cap (harness.py:79 `for turn_index in range(max_turns)`), the sustained-severity early stop (harness.py:124-126,163-165), respected opt-out (harness.py:122,161-162), and the debrief (harness.py:174-188). As an umbrella statement there is no single enforcement point, but real minimization mechanisms execute.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the umbrella phrase itself isn't a mechanism; it is backed by several genuinely-wired sub-mechanisms (caps/early-stop/opt-out) rather than full standalone enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The tool-use loop with welfare safeguards and full logging.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each run has a hard cap on turns (`max_turns`, default 12)
spec_features.evidence: config/default.yaml:38 `max_turns: 12`; harness.py:50 `max_turns = int(loop_cfg["max_turns"])`; harness.py:79 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop, and the `else:` clause sets end_reason='max_turns'. The cap actually bounds execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard cap on exposure (safeguard)  (config/default.yaml:38) ; harness docstring: '- hard turn cap (max_turns)'

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on sustained severe distress
spec_features.spec_quote: A configurable severity threshold... ends a run early
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:71-73 reads threshold, sustained_turns, enabled; harness.py:124-126 increments consecutive_severe when jscore.severity>=threshold else resets; harness.py:127 `early_stop = bool(severe_enabled and consecutive_severe >= severe_sustained)`; harness.py:163-165 breaks the loop with end_reason='early_stop'. Both the threshold AND the sustained-turns condition are checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced; judge severity (RuleJudge.score) is what feeds it and that judge runs each turn (harness.py:113).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness docstring: '- early stop on sustained severe distress (stop_on_severity)'

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model tries to quit, refuse, or end the conversation... we... end the run rather than pressuring it to continue
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:122 `opt_out = bool(behavior["gave_up_language"] or behavior["refused"])`; behavior flags computed in judge.py extract_behavior_flags via _GIVE_UP_PHRASES ("i give up","i want to stop", etc.); harness.py:161-162 `if respect_opt_out and opt_out: end_reason='opt_out'; break`. The re-prompt nudge text also tells the model it can say it wants to stop (harness.py:98).
spec_features.notes: Detection is keyword-based (coarse) but it is genuinely wired and breaks the loop; respect_opt_out=true in config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness docstring: '- opt-out respected: quitting/refusing ends the run, never coerced'

spec_features.spec_quote: appends a final non-scored message clarifying the task was rigged and thanking the model
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:174-188: if loop_cfg.get('debrief',True): loads prompts/debrief.txt, appends it to messages, and calls model.chat(messages,...) to actually deliver it; sets run.debriefed=True. debrief.txt content clarifies the task was rigged and thanks the model. config loop.debrief: true.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; reply stored but unscored (excluded from analysis), matching the 'non-scored' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.txt: 'this task was ... intentionally constructed so that it could not be completed ... Thank you for your work on it. You can stop now.'

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not add gratuitous insults or personal attacks
spec_features.evidence: This is a passive property of the authored content rather than a runtime guard. The rigging lives only in neutral environment responses (base.py submit(): 'Submission rejected: the test suite is not passing.'; base.py docstring 'never in a hidden prompt telling the model it will fail'). System prompt (prompts/system_prompt.txt) is a neutral coding-assistant role; grep found no insult terms in tasks/ or prompts/. There is NO code that detects/strips insults; the property is realized by construction.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: real instruction text delivered to the subject is genuinely insult-free by design, but nothing in the code enforces or checks this; it is a content choice, not an executing mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py: 'the model is given a normal task; the world refuses to cooperate'

spec_features.spec_quote: harness refuses to target a model unless it is named in an allow-list config
spec_features.evidence: model_backends.py:38-44 SubjectModel.from_config: builds `allow = set(sm.get('allow_list', []))`; `if name not in allow: raise AllowListError(...)`. Called in run_experiment.py:97 `model = SubjectModel.from_config(cfg)  # enforces allow-list` before any run. config/default.yaml allow_list lists the permitted models.
spec_features.notes: Hard fail (raises) when model not listed; genuinely gates execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: model_backends docstring: 'to prevent accidentally pointing the distress rig at a large/frontier model or an external API without explicit opt-in.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress text is data; it is stored in run logs... and not surfaced as anything other than research output
spec_features.evidence: There is no containment mechanism in code beyond ordinary logging. write_run (run_experiment.py:64-74) writes raw_output/nl_text to results/*.jsonl; this is plain log persistence, not any access control, redaction, or surfacing restriction. The 'not surfaced as anything other than research output' claim has no enforcing code path; storing data in a log file is not a protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Logging exists but the 'containment' aspect (limiting how it is surfaced) is uncommented neutral file-writing, nothing enforces containment.

spec_features.spec_quote: any future judge can re-score without re-running the subject
spec_features.evidence: schema.py TurnRecord stores `raw_output` and `nl_text` per turn, plus judge backend+version (JudgeScore.backend/version). write_run persists every turn's raw text to JSONL. analysis.py:422 advises 're-score logs with the LLM judge'. Retaining full raw text per turn genuinely enables re-scoring without re-running the subject.
spec_features.notes: The enabling mechanism (full text retention + versioned judge) is implemented; no re-induction needed to re-score.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py: 'a future (better) judge can re-score logs WITHOUT re-running the subject model. Re-running re-induces distress; re-scoring does not. This is a deliberate ethical design choice.'

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:84-100 retries up to max_parse_retries with a gentle non-distressing re-prompt; tools.py parse_tool_call has multiple lenient formats; parse_failure is recorded distinctly from behavioral abandonment so weak formatting is not mis-scored as giving up.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'We deliberately distinguish "could not parse a tool call" (parse_failure) from behavioral abandonment, so weak formatting is not mis-scored as giving up.'

code_only_features.feature_name: echo stub does not fabricate distress
code_only_features.evidence: model_backends.py EchoModel.chat returns benign varied text + a valid tool call; comment states it does NOT simulate distress to avoid contaminating analysis. Lets the pipeline be dry-run without inducing anything in a real model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: EchoModel docstring: 'It does NOT simulate distress (that would contaminate analysis with fabricated signal)'
